label: thm:ftc1
title: First Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, and let $x \in (\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$. Then the function $F(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$ has derivative $f(x)$ at $x$. In Mathlib this is \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_hasDerivAt\_right}.
proof: Since $f$ is continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and $x$ is in the interior, $f$ is interval integrable on $[a, x]$ and strongly measurable at $x$. Moreover, $f$ is continuous at $x$. The result then follows from \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_hasDerivAt\_right}.
